facts.text: North Westminster emerged as a northern village cluster tied to early agrarian expansion and small-scale industries like woolen mills and basket manufacturing.
The Gageville Covered Bridge, built in 1835 over the Saxtons River, is a historic Town truss design spanning 118 feet.
North Westminster surrendered its charter as an incorporated village on April 20, 2010, and reverted to the town of Westminster.
The North Westminster Community House serves as a central gathering space for local events and volunteer initiatives.
Average January lows in North Westminster hover around 10 degrees Fahrenheit, reflecting the influence of the surrounding New England highlands.
Sidney Gage and Company was a prominent basket manufacturing enterprise that influenced the local economy of North Westminster during the 19th century.
